lifetime_conclusions: Registry lookup gives a borrowed pointer; pointer nonnull, valid numeric ID and SoftLinkable alive are different from registered/not-retiring.
Released numeric IDs can be chosen again immediately if they are the available choice. External AI caches need identity/lifetime policy beyond these IDs.
Registration, explicit rekey, numeric setter and class setter have different side effects; numeric setters alone do not repair lookup maps.
Normal deferred drain and enqueue rely on external phase/quiescence invariants; enqueue mutex alone does not make drain concurrent-safe.
No runtime hooks, ABI calls, game execution or script-extender changes have been performed.
open_static_leads: Frame event-router ownership, worker join/quiescence, drain reentrancy and full reference-release producer invariants.
Ownership/player setter7EEEC0 and its derived slot19/56, brain19, group9304A0, sensor873810 and weaponry807A10 effects; follow flag producers.
ActorID setterevent2C derived chassis slot59; registration/rekey caller input constraints and post-load remap users beyond scoped caller census.
Scene entity enumeration lifecycle and component replacement/factory completeness; prior retirement map supplies pending-delete cleanup and SoftLinkable final invalidation.
Broader frontier: squad coordination, threat/attacking flag producers, suppression/morale, remaining action families and material/guidance/native scripting contracts.
